Gender Data is data regarding relationships in status, roles, and conditions between men and women. 31. Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of Gender and Child Data consisting of components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/institutions and regions in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of Gender Responsive and Child-sensitive development. 32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 33. Family Quality is the condition of the Family determined by the dimensions of quality of legality and structure, quality of physical resilience, quality of economic resilience, quality of socio-psychological resilience, and quality of socio-cultural resilience in realizing Gender Equality and Child's Rights. 34. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and preventing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 35. Violence Against Women hereinafter abbreviated as KTP is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 36. Violence Against Children hereinafter abbreviated as KTA is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom. 37. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household. 38. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 39. Exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits. 40. Witness and/or Victim is a witness who is also a victim who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, resulting from the criminal act of human trafficking. 41. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 42. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority as Parents over a Child. 43. Business World is micro enterprises, small enterprises, medium enterprises, and large enterprises that conduct economic activities in Indonesia and are domiciled in Indonesia. 44. Community is individuals, families, groups, mass media, business world, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 45. Community Participation is the participation of community members to channel their aspirations, thoughts, and interests in the administration of Regional Government. 46. Community Organization hereinafter referred to as Ormas is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities, and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 47. Social Conflict hereinafter referred to as Conflict is a feud and/or physical clash with Violence between two or more community groups that lasts for a certain time and has broad impacts resulting in insecurity and social disintegration thus disrupting national stability and hindering national development. 48.

Article 27

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One Definitions

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Area is the Sumedang Regency Area. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally. 16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that impacts, or has similar impacts on physical, psychological, and sexual aspects or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 24. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child's Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal, and other actions to ensure that Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, rights to family environment and alternative care, rights to basic health and welfare, as well as rights to education, use of leisure time, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child's Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

Article 62 Paragraph (1)

Point a What is meant by "Children in Emergency Situations" are Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disrupts the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.

Point b What is meant by "Children in Conflict with the Law" are Children in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts.

Point c What is meant by "Children from Minority and Isolated Groups" are Children who are left behind, at the forefront, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, ethnicity, race, religion from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups.

What is meant by "Children Who Are Sexually Exploited" are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecent acts.

Point e What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse" are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.

Point f What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Pornography" are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes.

Point g What is meant by "Children with HIV and AIDS" are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Trafficking" are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or internationally, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited.

Point i What is meant by "Child Victims of Physical Violence" are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Psychological Violence" are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering.

Point j What is meant by "Child Victims of Sexual Crimes" are Children who experience forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point k What is meant by "Child Victims of Terrorism Networks" are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by acts of terrorism either as child victims, child perpetrators, children of perpetrators, and child witnesses.

Point 1 What is meant by "Children with Disabilities" are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.

Point m What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.

Point o What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to Their Parents' Condition" are Children who are given negative social labels based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing Children with a stigma or bad view from labeling related to their parents' condition.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in social, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women’s empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women’s Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women’s empowerment and protection, child protection, and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish it by Regional Regulation.

Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally. 16. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that impacts, or has similar impacts on physical, psychological, and sexual aspects or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 24. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child's Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal, and other actions to ensure that Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, rights to family environment and alternative care, rights to basic health and welfare, as well as rights to education, use of leisure time, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child's Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in social, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women’s empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women’s Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women’s empowerment and protection, child protection, and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish it by Regional Regulation.

Article 51

1. The Regency Government, Community, Family, and Parents or Guardians are obligated and responsible for the administration of Child Protection in the Regency Area.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in social, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women’s empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women’s Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women’s empowerment and protection, child protection, and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish it by Regional Regulation.

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally. 16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that impacts, or has similar impacts on physical, psychological, and sexual aspects or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 24. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child's Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal, and other actions to ensure that Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, rights to family environment and alternative care, rights to basic health and welfare, as well as rights to education, use of leisure time, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child's Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

Article 62 Paragraph (1)

Point a What is meant by "Children in Emergency Situations" are Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disrupts the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.

Point b What is meant by "Children in Conflict with the Law" are Children in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts.

Point c What is meant by "Children from Minority and Isolated Groups" are Children who are left behind, at the forefront, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, ethnicity, race, religion from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups.

Point d What is meant by "Children Who Are Economically Exploited" are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.

What is meant by "Children Who Are Sexually Exploited" are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecent acts.

Point e What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse" are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.

Point f What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Pornography" are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes.

Point g What is meant by "Children with HIV and AIDS" are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.

Point h What is meant by "Child Victims of Abduction" are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Sale" are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to another party for compensation or other reasons.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Trafficking" are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or internationally, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited.

Point i What is meant by "Child Victims of Physical Violence" are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Psychological Violence" are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering.

Point j What is meant by "Child Victims of Sexual Crimes" are Children who experience forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point k What is meant by "Child Victims of Terrorism Networks" are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by acts of terrorism either as child victims, child perpetrators, children of perpetrators, and child witnesses.

Point 1 What is meant by "Children with Disabilities" are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.

Point m What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.

Point n What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.

What is meant by Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child, resulting in harm to the Child's growth and development process.

Point o What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to Their Parents' Condition" are Children who are given negative social labels based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing Children with a stigma or bad view from labeling related to their parents' condition.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in social, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women’s empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women’s Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women’s empowerment and protection, child protection, and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish it by Regional Regulation.

3. building cooperation on KTP prevention involving parties in the Regency Area.
b. policy advocacy and service assistance for Women's Protection in the Regency Area, covering:

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in social, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women’s empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women’s Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women’s empowerment and protection, child protection, and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish it by Regional Regulation.

Article 51

1. The Regency Government, Community, Family, and Parents or Guardians are obligated and responsible for the administration of Child Protection in the Regency Area.
2. Obligations and responsibilities of the Regency Government in implementing the administration of Child Protection in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. respecting the Fulfillment of Children's Rights without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status, birth order, and physical and/or mental condition;
b. implementing and supporting national policies in the administration of Child protection in the Regency Area; and
c. providing support for facilities, infrastructure, and availability of human resources in the administration of Child Protection in the Regency Area.
3. The Regency Government in carrying out obligations and responsibilities in Child Protection in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be implemented by:
a. guaranteeing the protection, care, and welfare of Children with due regard to the rights and obligations of Parents, Guardians, or other persons who are legally responsible for the Child; and
b. supervising the implementation of the administration of Child Protection in the Regency Area.

Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 24. I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in social, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women’s empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women’s Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women’s empowerment and protection, child protection, and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish it by Regional Regulation.

Article 100

1. The Regency Regional Government may establish an evaluation Team in conducting evaluation of the administration of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. The establishment of the evaluation team as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent Decree.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out annually.
3. The results of the evaluation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection become input material in the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the coming year.
4. Further provisions regarding monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of the administration of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1), are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 33

Further provisions regarding the Protection of Women from GBV in disasters as referred to in Article 31 and Article 32, shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation, guided by laws and regulations governing disaster management.

Part One Definitions

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally. 16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that impacts, or has similar impacts on physical, psychological, and sexual aspects or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 24. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Paragraph 3

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in social, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women’s empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women’s Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women’s empowerment and protection, child protection, and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish it by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in social, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women’s empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women’s Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women’s empowerment and protection, child protection, and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish it by Regional Regulation.

Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of Gender and Child Data consisting of components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/institutions and regions in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of Gender Responsive and Child-sensitive development. 32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 33. Family Quality is the condition of the Family determined by the dimensions of quality of legality and structure, quality of physical resilience, quality of economic resilience, quality of socio-psychological resilience, and quality of socio-cultural resilience in realizing Gender Equality and Child's Rights. 34. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and preventing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 35. Violence Against Women hereinafter abbreviated as KTP is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 36. Violence Against Children hereinafter abbreviated as KTA is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom. 37. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household. 38. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 39. Exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits. 40. Witness and/or Victim is a witness who is also a victim who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, resulting from the criminal act of human trafficking. 41. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 42. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority as Parents over a Child. 43. Business World is micro enterprises, small enterprises, medium enterprises, and large enterprises that conduct economic activities in Indonesia and are domiciled in Indonesia. 44. Community is individuals, families, groups, mass media, business world, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 45. Community Participation is the participation of community members to channel their aspirations, thoughts, and interests in the administration of Regional Government. 46. Community Organization hereinafter referred to as Ormas is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities, and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 47. Social Conflict hereinafter referred to as Conflict is a feud and/or physical clash with Violence between two or more community groups that lasts for a certain time and has broad impacts resulting in insecurity and social disintegration thus disrupting national stability and hindering national development. 48.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One Definitions

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Area is the Sumedang Regency Area. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally. 16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that impacts, or has similar impacts on physical, psychological, and sexual aspects or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 24. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child's Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal, and other actions to ensure that Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, rights to family environment and alternative care, rights to basic health and welfare, as well as rights to education, use of leisure time, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One Definitions

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Area is the Sumedang Regency Area. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally. 16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One Definitions

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Area is the Sumedang Regency Area. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in social, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women’s empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women’s Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women’s empowerment and protection, child protection, and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish it by Regional Regulation.

c. strengthening and development of Women's Protection Service Provider Institutions in the Regency Area.

Article 62 Paragraph (1)

Point a What is meant by "Children in Emergency Situations" are Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disrupts the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.

Point b What is meant by "Children in Conflict with the Law" are Children in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts.

Point c What is meant by "Children from Minority and Isolated Groups" are Children who are left behind, at the forefront, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, ethnicity, race, religion from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups.

Point d What is meant by "Children Who Are Economically Exploited" are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.

What is meant by "Children Who Are Sexually Exploited" are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecent acts.

Point e What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse" are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.

Point f What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Pornography" are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes.

Point g What is meant by "Children with HIV and AIDS" are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.

Point h What is meant by "Child Victims of Abduction" are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Sale" are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to another party for compensation or other reasons.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Trafficking" are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or internationally, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited.

Point i What is meant by "Child Victims of Physical Violence" are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Psychological Violence" are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering.

Point j What is meant by "Child Victims of Sexual Crimes" are Children who experience forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point k What is meant by "Child Victims of Terrorism Networks" are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by acts of terrorism either as child victims, child perpetrators, children of perpetrators, and child witnesses.

Point 1 What is meant by "Children with Disabilities" are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.

Point m What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.

Point n What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.

What is meant by Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child, resulting in harm to the Child's growth and development process.

Point o What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to Their Parents' Condition" are Children who are given negative social labels based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing Children with a stigma or bad view from labeling related to their parents' condition.
