CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One Definitions

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Area is the Sumedang Regency Area. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally. 16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that impacts, or has similar impacts on physical, psychological, and sexual aspects or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 24. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child's Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal, and other actions to ensure that Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, rights to family environment and alternative care, rights to basic health and welfare, as well as rights to education, use of leisure time, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child's Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One Definitions

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Area is the Sumedang Regency Area. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally. 16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that impacts, or has similar impacts on physical, psychological, and sexual aspects or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 24. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child's Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal, and other actions to ensure that Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, rights to family environment and alternative care, rights to basic health and welfare, as well as rights to education, use of leisure time, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child's Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and Children who experience Violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 49. Children's Forum is a forum for Child Participation where its members are representatives of children's groups or children's activity groups or individuals, and are fostered by the government, as a means of channeling the aspirations, voices, opinions, desires, and needs of Children in the development process. 50. Family Learning Center hereinafter referred to as Puspaga is a learning place to improve the quality of family life carried out by professional personnel through capacity building of Parents/Families or persons responsible for children in carrying out the responsibility of caring for and protecting children so as to create the need for affection, attachment, safety, and welfare that is stable and sustainable for the best interests of the child, including protection from Violence, exploitation, abuse and neglect. 51. Women's Empowerment Service Provider Institution is a government-owned institution or a legal community institution that makes efforts to improve the quality of life and active Participation of women in development, both in the implementation of policies, activities, and administration in the provision of services. 52. Service Provider Institution for Children Requiring Special Protection hereinafter referred to as Service Provider Institution for AMPK is a government-owned institution or a legal community institution that provides services for AMPK and other problems both in the implementation of policies, activities, and administration. 53. Service Provider Institution for Improving the Quality of Life of Children is a government-owned institution or a legal community institution that makes efforts to improve the quality of life of Children both in the implementation of policies, activities, and administration in the provision of services. 54. Service Provider Institution for Improving Family Quality is a government-owned institution or a legal community institution that makes efforts to improve Family Quality both in the implementation of policies, activities, and administration in the provision of services. 55. Service Standards are benchmarks and guidelines for the provision of public services as well as references for assessing service quality as obligations and promises of providers to the community in the context of services in a fast, accurate, comprehensive and integrated manner. 56. Social Rehabilitation is the recovery of witnesses and/or victims from psychosocial condition disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning both in the family and in the community. 57. Repatriation is the act of returning witnesses and/or victims to their area of origin or country of origin while prioritizing protection services and fulfillment of their needs. 58. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing Children who require Special Protection to be able to return to the family and community environment. 59. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJPD is a regional development planning document with a period of 20 (twenty) years, which contains the vision, mission, and direction of regional development that refers to the National Long-Term Development Plan and the West Java Provincial Long-Term Development Plan. 60. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD is a Regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years from the inauguration until the end of the Regent's term of office. 61. Regional Annual Development Plan hereinafter referred to as Regional Government Work Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RKPD is a Regional planning document for a period of 1 (one) year. 62. Regional Apparatus Strategic Plan hereinafter referred to as Renstra is a Regional Apparatus planning document for a period of 5 (five) years. 63. Regional Apparatus Work Plan hereinafter referred to as Renja is a Regional Apparatus planning document for a period of 1 (one) year.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in social, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women’s empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women’s Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women’s empowerment and protection, child protection, and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish it by Regional Regulation.

3. Further provisions regarding the Implementation of CFC as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by a separate Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in social, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women’s empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women’s Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women’s empowerment and protection, child protection, and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish it by Regional Regulation.

a. implementation of policies, programs, and activities; and

1. Improvement of Family Quality in realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in the Regency Area, is implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.

a. institutional;

c. synergy and coordination; and
d. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.

a. policy advocacy and family assistance to realize Gender Equality and Children's Rights in the Regency Area include:

3. increasing Community Participation and mass media in improving Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights; and
4. strengthening cooperation of Regency Regional Apparatus to realize Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights.
b. implementation of communication, information, and education on Gender Equality and Children's Rights for Families in the Regency Area; and
c. development of Community activities for improving Family Quality in the Regency Area.

Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that impacts, or has similar impacts on physical, psychological, and sexual aspects or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 24. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child's Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal, and other actions to ensure that Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, rights to family environment and alternative care, rights to basic health and welfare, as well as rights to education, use of leisure time, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child's Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in social, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women’s empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women’s Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women’s empowerment and protection, child protection, and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish it by Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One Definitions

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Area is the Sumedang Regency Area. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally. 16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that impacts, or has similar impacts on physical, psychological, and sexual aspects or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 24. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child's Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal, and other actions to ensure that Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, rights to family environment and alternative care, rights to basic health and welfare, as well as rights to education, use of leisure time, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child's Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and Children who experience Violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 49. Children's Forum is a forum for Child Participation where its members are representatives of children's groups or children's activity groups or individuals, and are fostered by the government, as a means of channeling the aspirations, voices, opinions, desires, and needs of Children in the development process. 50. Family Learning Center hereinafter referred to as Puspaga is a learning place to improve the quality of family life carried out by professional personnel through capacity building of Parents/Families or persons responsible for children in carrying out the responsibility of caring for and protecting children so as to create the need for affection, attachment, safety, and welfare that is stable and sustainable for the best interests of the child, including protection from Violence, exploitation, abuse and neglect. 51. Women's Empowerment Service Provider Institution is a government-owned institution or a legal community institution that makes efforts to improve the quality of life and active Participation of women in development, both in the implementation of policies, activities, and administration in the provision of services. 52. Service Provider Institution for Children Requiring Special Protection hereinafter referred to as Service Provider Institution for AMPK is a government-owned institution or a legal community institution that provides services for AMPK and other problems both in the implementation of policies, activities, and administration. 53. Service Provider Institution for Improving the Quality of Life of Children is a government-owned institution or a legal community institution that makes efforts to improve the quality of life of Children both in the implementation of policies, activities, and administration in the provision of services. 54. Service Provider Institution for Improving Family Quality is a government-owned institution or a legal community institution that makes efforts to improve Family Quality both in the implementation of policies, activities, and administration in the provision of services. 55. Service Standards are benchmarks and guidelines for the provision of public services as well as references for assessing service quality as obligations and promises of providers to the community in the context of services in a fast, accurate, comprehensive and integrated manner. 56. Social Rehabilitation is the recovery of witnesses and/or victims from psychosocial condition disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning both in the family and in the community. 57. Repatriation is the act of returning witnesses and/or victims to their area of origin or country of origin while prioritizing protection services and fulfillment of their needs. 58. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing Children who require Special Protection to be able to return to the family and community environment. 59. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJPD is a regional development planning document with a period of 20 (twenty) years, which contains the vision, mission, and direction of regional development that refers to the National Long-Term Development Plan and the West Java Provincial Long-Term Development Plan. 60. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD is a Regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years from the inauguration until the end of the Regent's term of office. 61. Regional Annual Development Plan hereinafter referred to as Regional Government Work Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RKPD is a Regional planning document for a period of 1 (one) year. 62. Regional Apparatus Strategic Plan hereinafter referred to as Renstra is a Regional Apparatus planning document for a period of 5 (five) years. 63. Regional Apparatus Work Plan hereinafter referred to as Renja is a Regional Apparatus planning document for a period of 1 (one) year.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in social, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women’s empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women’s Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women’s empowerment and protection, child protection, and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish it by Regional Regulation.

Article 58

1. Strengthening and development of Service Provider Institutions for Improving the Quality of Life of Children in the Regency Area as referred to in Article 53 letter b is implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
2. Standards for strengthening and development of Service Provider Institutions for Improving the Quality of Life of Children in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. Procedures for strengthening and development as referred to in paragraph (1) consist of:
a. provision of services for improving the quality of life of Children in the Regency Area;
b. coordination and synchronization of the implementation of assistance for improving the quality of life of Children in the Regency Area;
c. development of communication, information, and education on the Fulfillment of Children's Rights for Service Provider Institutions for Improving the Quality of Life of Children in the Regency Area; and
d. strengthening networks among Service Provider Institutions for Improving the Quality of Life of Children in the Regency Area.

Part Two Improvement of Family Quality in Realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in the Regency Area

Article 83 Improvement of Family Quality in realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in the Regency Area, is implemented through:
a. implementation of policies, programs, and activities; and
b. development of materials and implementation of communication, information, and education on Gender Equality and Children's Rights for Families.
1. Improvement of Family Quality in realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in the Regency Area, is implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
2. Standards for improving Family Quality as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. institutional;
b. availability of communication, information, education materials;
c. synergy and coordination; and
d. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.
3. Procedures for improving Family Quality as referred to in paragraph (1) consist of:
a. policy advocacy and family assistance to realize Gender Equality and Children's Rights in the Regency Area include:
1. preparation of planning and budgeting documents for Family Quality that realize Gender Equality and Children's Rights;
2. coordination and synchronization of policy formulation for Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights;
3. increasing Community Participation and mass media in improving Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights; and
4. strengthening cooperation of Regency Regional Apparatus to realize Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights.
b. implementation of communication, information, and education on Gender Equality and Children's Rights for Families in the Regency Area; and
c. development of Community activities for improving Family Quality in the Regency Area.

Article 100

1. The Regency Regional Government may establish an evaluation Team in conducting evaluation of the administration of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. The establishment of the evaluation team as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent Decree.

3. The results of the evaluation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection become input material in the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the coming year.

Children Requiring Special Protection hereinafter abbreviated as AMPK are Children in emergency situations, Children in conflict with the law, Children from minority and isolated groups, Children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, Children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse, Children who are victims of pornography, Children with HIV/AIDS, Children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, and/or trafficking, Children who are victims of physical and/or psychological violence, Children who are victims of sexual crimes, Children who are victims of terrorism networks, Children with disabilities, Children who are victims of abuse and neglect, Children with deviant social behavior, and Children who are victims of stigmatization from labeling related to their parents' condition, and Children with other problems. 30. Gender Data is data regarding relationships in status, roles, and conditions between men and women. 31. Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of Gender and Child Data consisting of components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/institutions and regions in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of Gender Responsive and Child-sensitive development. 32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 33. Family Quality is the condition of the Family determined by the dimensions of quality of legality and structure, quality of physical resilience, quality of economic resilience, quality of socio-psychological resilience, and quality of socio-cultural resilience in realizing Gender Equality and Child's Rights. 34. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and preventing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 35. Violence Against Women hereinafter abbreviated as KTP is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 36. Violence Against Children hereinafter abbreviated as KTA is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom. 37. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household. 38. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 39. Exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits. 40. Witness and/or Victim is a witness who is also a victim who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, resulting from the criminal act of human trafficking. 41. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 42. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority as Parents over a Child. 43. Business World is micro enterprises, small enterprises, medium enterprises, and large enterprises that conduct economic activities in Indonesia and are domiciled in Indonesia. 44. Community is individuals, families, groups, mass media, business world, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 45. Community Participation is the participation of community members to channel their aspirations, thoughts, and interests in the administration of Regional Government. 46. Community Organization hereinafter referred to as Ormas is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities, and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 47. Social Conflict hereinafter referred to as Conflict is a feud and/or physical clash with Violence between two or more community groups that lasts for a certain time and has broad impacts resulting in insecurity and social disintegration thus disrupting national stability and hindering national development. 48.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One Definitions

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Area is the Sumedang Regency Area. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally. 16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that impacts, or has similar impacts on physical, psychological, and sexual aspects or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 24. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child's Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal, and other actions to ensure that Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, rights to family environment and alternative care, rights to basic health and welfare, as well as rights to education, use of leisure time, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child's Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government; however, in reality the position of women and children in social, national, and state life is still placed as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, and enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women’s empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of concurrent government affairs that are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women’s Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women’s empowerment and protection, child protection, and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order, and to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish it by Regional Regulation.

Part Two Improvement of Family Quality in Realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in the Regency Area

Article 83 Improvement of Family Quality in realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in the Regency Area, is implemented through:
a. implementation of policies, programs, and activities; and
b. development of materials and implementation of communication, information, and education on Gender Equality and Children's Rights for Families.
1. Improvement of Family Quality in realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in the Regency Area, is implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
2. Standards for improving Family Quality as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. institutional;
b. availability of communication, information, education materials;
c. synergy and coordination; and
d. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.
3. Procedures for improving Family Quality as referred to in paragraph (1) consist of:
a. policy advocacy and family assistance to realize Gender Equality and Children's Rights in the Regency Area include:
1. preparation of planning and budgeting documents for Family Quality that realize Gender Equality and Children's Rights;
2. coordination and synchronization of policy formulation for Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights;
3. increasing Community Participation and mass media in improving Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights; and
4. strengthening cooperation of Regency Regional Apparatus to realize Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights.
b. implementation of communication, information, and education on Gender Equality and Children's Rights for Families in the Regency Area; and
c. development of Community activities for improving Family Quality in the Regency Area.
